intervals.label: construction begins
intervals.locator: JLab news story "Fifteen Years of Beam on Target", section "Great Expectations"
intervals.note: Jefferson Lab gives the month (February 1987) for the start of construction; no official page consulted states a day.
intervals.quote: Construction on what came to be called the Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility began in February of 1987

intervals.label: 12 GeV Upgrade dedication
intervals.locator: JLab Archives page, closing paragraph of the history summary
intervals.note: This is the dedication ceremony; earlier operation is recorded in the first-beam (1994), 4 GeV (1995) and 6 GeV (2000) intervals.
intervals.quote: On Wednesday, May 2, 2018, the CEBAF 12 GeV Upgrade Dedication Ceremony took place

intervals.label: first beam delivered to an experimental hall
intervals.locator: JLab news story "Fifteen Years of Beam on Target", opening paragraph
intervals.quote: On July 1, 1994, Jefferson Lab's accelerator delivered an electron beam into one of its experimental halls for the first time.

intervals.label: 4 GeV design energy achieved
intervals.locator: JLab news story "Fifteen Years of Beam on Target", section "Great Expectations"
intervals.note: This is CEBAF's original design energy before either the 6 GeV or 12 GeV upgrades. Jefferson Lab gives the month, November 1995 (its operations-orientation page gives the year, 1995).
intervals.quote: The machine reached full-design energy, 4 GeV, in November 1995.

beam_energy.note: Same statement as the interval itself.
beam_energy.quote: The machine reached full-design energy, 4 GeV, in November 1995.

intervals.label: 6 GeV beam delivered (6.07 GeV)
intervals.note: Jefferson Lab's archive gives the month, August 2000, and the energy delivered, 6.07 GeV (150% of the original CEBAF energy). This is the 6 GeV operation that preceded the 12 GeV upgrade; no official page consulted gives a day.
intervals.quote: In August 2000, the accelerator delivered 6.07 GeV (billion electron volts), 150% of the original CEBAF energy.

beam_energy.quote: In August 2000, the accelerator delivered 6.07 GeV (billion electron volts), 150% of the original CEBAF energy.

name: Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility
notes: kind is recorded as `linac`; CEBAF is technically a recirculating (racetrack) superconducting linac, which ACCELERATOR_KINDS does not have a dedicated value for.

CEBAF's original operating history (first beam 1994-07-01, 4 GeV design energy 1995-11, 6.07 GeV in 2000-08) is sourced to Jefferson Lab's news story and archives page, as are the 1987 construction start (month precision) and the 2018 12 GeV dedication.

beam_energy.note: Original design energy was 4 GeV (6 GeV from 2000); the 12 GeV Upgrade was dedicated 2 May 2018 (see the 2018-05-02 interval).
beam_energy.quote: The CEBAF energy was recently upgraded from 6 GeV to 12 GeV, and an additional experimental area was added to support the highest-energy experiments.

summary.plain: Jefferson Lab's main particle accelerator, which fires a continuous beam of electrons at nuclear targets in three (now four) experimental halls. It began at 4 GeV, was raised to 6 GeV in 2000, and was upgraded again to 12 GeV in 2018.
summary.technical: Continuous Electron Beam Accelerator Facility: a superconducting recirculating (racetrack) electron linac at Jefferson Lab; first beam 1994-07-01, reached its 4 GeV design energy in November 1995, delivered 6.07 GeV in August 2000, and runs at 12 GeV after the Upgrade dedicated 2018-05-02.
